thread.title: Why investors should bet on a Facebook comeback

author: morningstar.com
title: Why investors should bet on a Facebook comeback
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
Facebook's recent data-breach prolongs a rough run of late for the social-media giant that is got investors wary over the next shoe to drop (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-horrible-week-for-facebook-somehow-gets-even-worse-2018-09-28).
The company is trailing its tech peers, otherwise known as the FAANG gang--Amazon, Apple (AAPL), Netflix, and Alphabet's Google (GOOGL)--in a big way. Zuck's company is down 9.7% year-to-date, while on the other end, Netflix (NFLX) is up 96%, followed by a 68% gain for Amazon (AMZN).
And that brings us to our call of the day, from CrackedMarket's Jani Ziedins who says if anyone can pull off a comeback, it is Zuck's pride and joy.
"This is still the hottest social media property and nothing else comes close. As long as technology continues to be the hottest sector, Facebook will continue to be a buy," he said. Out of 48 analysts tracked on FactSet, two rated Facebook a sell, seven a hold, with the rest buy or overweight ratings.
"At this point, FB is far more likely to catch up to the other tech highfliers than it is to bring everyone else down to their level," Ziedins says, though he cautions that while things look still look OK for the company near term and into year-end, "the situation could look a lot different next year."
Facebook: Hackers didn't access other apps in breach that affected 50 million accounts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-hackers-did-not-access-other-apps-with-login-2018-10-02)
Nonetheless, all that glitters doesn't do that forever. Or something like that. And eventually, as happens to every hot sector at some point, is that the baton will be handed over to the next dazzling group of stocks, Ziedins reminds us.
Read: This might be the riskiest sector of the U.S. stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-might-be-the-riskiest-sector-of-the-us-stock-market-2018-10-01)
The market
Reports that Italy's will toe the Brussels line over its budget woes are easing worries about another euro-area crisis. Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are just in the green after Tuesday's action that saw the Dow nail the 14th record this year. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite finished lower.
The euro is up (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/euro-rebounds-after-report-italy-will-play-by-eus-budget-deficit-rules-2018-10-03), with Europe stocks in the green, led by the FTSE MIB Italy index . Asia had a flat session (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-hang-seng-about-flat-after-making-up-early-losses-2018-10-02).
Elsewhere, gold is flat and crude is higher.
Check out the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-could-carve-out-record-as-italy-fears-fade-2018-10-03) for the latest action.
The chart
How tight are they? Our chart of the day taps into what's turned into some financial water-cooler talk lately, that is the spread between the average yield on a junk bond and that of U.S. government bonds.
According to Bloomberg, that spread is now the lowest since 2007. For investors, the time to grab those junk bonds is usually when that spread is wide and they're getting more bang for their buck against play-it-safe government bonds. So when investors are willing to take the extra risk for less money, eyebrows are raised.
(https://twitter.com/lisaabramowicz1/status/1047103096541859840)
The buzz
Facebook definitely doesn't need more problems, but it #instagramdown (https://twitter.com/hashtag/instagramdown?src=tren) has been a top trender in the wee hours with what looks like an outage in some parts of the world. Some on Twitter haven't been exactly welcoming to the Instagram refugees:
(https://twitter.com/andylassner/status/1047395901356920832)
New York authorities are looking into a report that claims President Donald Trump and his family schemed to help their parents dodge millions in taxes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/new-york-launches-tax-investigation-into-trump-after-ny-times-report-2018-10-02). He pocketed at least $413 million in today's dollars from his father Fred's real-estate business, the New York Times reported.
Tesla (TSLA) ended up with a worse deal than the SEC first offered. Here's how that happened. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-teslas-elon-musk-got-a-worse-deal-than-the-sec-first-offered-2018-10-02)

Luxury auto maker of James Bond fame, Aston Martin, got off to a soggy debut in London (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/aston-martin-ipo-values-james-bond-carmaker-at-56-billion-2018-10-03), with shares down 6% and well under that 1,900 pence IPO price.

The economy
Ahead of the open, we'll get ADP employment, followed by the Markit services purchasing managers index and the Institute for Supply Management's nonmanufacturing index.
And a boatload of Fed speakers are en route--Chicago Fed President Charles Evans, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin, Fed Gov Lael Brainard, Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester, and rounding things off, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell will make an appearance at an Atlantic magazine conference in Washington at 4 p.m. Eastern.
The Quote:
(https://twitter.com/BBCWorld/status/1047425481904193540)
"How did you get home? 'I don't remember.' How did you get there? 'I don't remember.' How many years ago was it? 'I don't know, I don't know, I don't know, I don't know.'"--That was POTUS, mocking the testimony of Christine BLASEY Ford (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-mocks-christine-blasey-fords-testimony-at-mississippi-rally-2018-10-02) at a rally in Mississippi, as he criticized her accusations of sexual assault against Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh for leaving his life in tatters.
The FBI probe into those allegations possibly could be wrapping up as soon as Wednesday (https://www.wsj.com/articles/with-uncertainty-in-gop-ranks-mcconnell-plans-votes-on-kavanaugh-1538486533?mod=hp_lead_pos1), with Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell pressing to get a vote on Kavanaugh as soon as possible.
